$schema_note: Hand-curated record of how Hero Siege announces a rare ground drop in chat, for ForgePact#17 (Loot announcements). NOT mechanically extracted (see hs-game-sdk/curated/satanic_zone.json for why curated/ exists). Data only: no binding is generated from this file. Every entry carries its own `status`: `static_reading` (read from the compiled game locally and paraphrased in our own words; no script text is kept anywhere), `inference`, `not_established`, or `measured` (`route.previous.status`, from ForgePact#17's Live procedure 3, `chat_line.measured_call`, from the dungeon chest's Live procedure 1b, and the parts of `chaos_tower_loot_burst` its `live` block lists, from capture forgepact-227-chaos-tower-announce-live-1; `route.status`, `route.live`, `chat_line.measured_colours` and the `seen_on_feed` of the `announcement_colours` entries for codes 9, 7 and 10 (the Satanic entry has none), from capture forgepact-228-loot-colors-live-1; `route.live2`, `chat_line.layout`, the `measured` fields of `chat_line.segments` and `announcement_sender_colour.seen_on_feed`, from capture forgepact-228-loot-colors-live-2). `route.status` `measured` covers the coloured line only: the fallback to the red server line ran in neither session (`route.live.not_run`, `route.live2.not_run`). `scripts` is the announcement chain by SDK name, in call order. `rarity_key` is the itemInfoStruct key the closure is taken to read: that key "27" holds the rarity is measured (docs/RUNTIME_DATA_MODELS.md section 16.4), but that the closure reads it is an inference from the codes it compares, because the key strings were not read. `rarity_codes_in_closure` lists every rarity code the closure compares on a branch of its own, and for each whether the online path announces it; the list is what was read, and `announced_online` is `not_established` where the reading does not say. `route` is the call ForgePact's `lootann` ships to show the line offline: `chatcolour` since ForgePact#228 (2026-10-23; ChatAddMessage by name in dungeon-chest shape 8's argument kinds, in the online announcement's layout: the character's name as the sender part in the online sender colour 18687 and 'found <item name>' as the text part in its rarity's announcement colour; `measured` since capture forgepact-228-loot-colors-live-1, which `route.live` records for an earlier layout, and the layout that ships measured in capture forgepact-228-loot-colors-live-2, `route.live2`), with `route.previous` the `server` route it replaced and now falls back to (chosen 2026-10-04 after Live procedures 1 and 3; the game's own path, `method`, could not be tested offline (the probe's anon control did not resolve)). `chat_line` (ForgePact#228) records how ChatAddMessage builds and draws a line: its fifteen parameters in order, the segments and their colours, the layout ForgePact ships (`layout`), and that a line carries two text colours and no inline markup. `rarity_colours` is the game's rarity colour table (GetRarityColor, codes 1-11), `announcement_colours` the text colour the online announcement passes per rarity, and `announcement_sender_colour` its sender colour. Colours are GameMaker's decimal blue-green-red integers (`bgr`) with `#RRGGBB` (`rgb`) beside them; docs/RUNTIME_DATA_MODELS.md sections 8.6 and 16.4 carry the same facts. The argument is ForgePact docs/loot-announcement-research.md; the shared facts are docs/RUNTIME_DATA_MODELS.md sections 8.6 and 16.10. `chaos_tower_loot_burst` (ForgePact#227) records how a Chaos Tower floor holds its new ground items in Controller_obj.lootExplosionList until gml_Script_LootExplosion puts them back on the ground at the floor's end (docs/RUNTIME_DATA_MODELS.md section 16.14), with its own `status` and a `not_established` list.

live.procedure: ForgePact#227's Live procedure 1 (the research doc's Live procedure 5): research build sha256 a21409cb7320811b8f337cf165f5ec3540cba8ec6a1bc147af68e8f1113a9fa3, slot 14 Sorak, Outskirts of Inoya at Hell, then Chaos_Tower_Floor_01_rm; read through lootannprobe burst, lootann stat and out.txt's lootann decide lines, with the owner watching the screen at the burst
measured: on the first floor, Controller_obj.lootExplosionList read as a reference to an existing ds_list whose size rose by one for each new ground item (4 natural drops before any placement, 1 in the frame of a placed Heroic item) and read 0 once the floor had ended
the listed natural drops' and the placed item's structs (with the list memory on) were built through CreateItemNew in that frame or the one before (burst-fresh rose with burst-listed)
GPV of Controller_obj.lootExplosionGiven read 0 while the floor collected and 1 once it had ended
the floor's end landed the held items: both placed items lay on the ground afterwards, each with the itemTimeStamp it had when listed, and burst-landed read 12

the struct that lands is the listed one, not a copy with the same itemTimeStamp: via=burst (B's announce, burst-landed=12) needs the landed item's key, which ForgePact derives from the item struct's object pointer, to equal a key kept when the entry was listed, and the list held that struct alive in between, so its pointer could not have been reused
the LootGroundInit detour saw each landed item twice (two lootann decide lines per stamp; 12 burst landings for the 6 kept entries); which two calls they were is not established

with the list memory off (the rule before ForgePact#227) a placed Heroic item was decided held-bag-drop at the burst and the owner saw no line; with it on, one was decided announce via=burst and the owner saw its red SERVER line
not_run: a bag drop on a floor (case C); the owner accepted the session without it
the LootExplosion debugger logpoint and the burst-window LootGroundInit logpoints (x64dbg paused the game on its own first-chance C++ exceptions during the floor's fight)
